subject: botany_2
question_text: Write any two differences between DNA and RNA.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.44, printed question 103. insider_note: The question asks for TWO, so give exactly two and make them sharp. Sugar and strandedness are the safest pair.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: First difference
steps.margin_note: Two clean differences, one per numbered pair.
steps.why: These two are structural facts that hold for every DNA and every RNA, so neither needs a qualification.
common_mistakes: Saying DNA has ribose. DNA has DEOXYribose — one oxygen less.
Saying RNA is double stranded. RNA is SINGLE stranded.
steps.memory_tip: Deoxy and double for DNA; ribose and single for RNA.

steps.label: Second difference
steps.margin_note: Two more differences. Four in total is more than the question asks for and costs nothing.

lines.text: DNA replicates itself; RNA does not

lines: RNA does NOT undergo self replication.
4. DNA has thymine; RNA has URACIL instead.
steps.why: Only DNA replicates because only DNA is the archive; RNA is made fresh from DNA each time it is needed.
common_mistakes: Saying RNA replicates in cells. It is transcribed from DNA, not self replicated.
Naming thymine in RNA. RNA has URACIL.
steps.memory_tip: One copies itself, the other is copied from it.
